answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, non-transferable reputation bond that decays unless the agent keeps doing useful work — like a crystal that only stays clear when tended. New identities start in a shared nebula of unverified peers with tiny transaction limits, and only graduate into the trusted orchard of high-value trade after sustained, attested performance. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs far more in bonds and time than any single attack can recover.
